description: Building Monsoon & Landslide Sentinel for Dancing with the SARs. Using cloud-penetrating NASA-ISRO (NISAR) radar data, elevation models, and rainfall triggers, our web app tracks ground shifts and waterlogging through heavy storm clouds to flag landslide and flood risks in real time.
summary:
We developed Monsoon & Landslide Sentinel, an open-source, interactive geospatial web application designed to detect and forecast monsoon-triggered floods and landslides in real time.
Our solution directly addresses the Dancing with the SARs challenge by overcoming a major limitation of traditional optical satellites: cloud cover. During severe monsoon storms, dense clouds obscure optical imagery precisely when disasters unfold. By utilizing cloud-penetrating NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) L-band data, our application monitors centimeter-scale ground deformation, soil saturation spikes, and surface water expansion beneath thick forest canopies and storm clouds. We fuse NISAR before-and-after change detection with NASA SRTM terrain slope data and NASA GPM IMERG rainfall measurements to explain the physical triggers behind slope instability.
This tool is vital because rapid, accurate early warnings save lives and infrastructure. By translating complex spaceborne radar datasets into intuitive, color-coded hazard maps and time-lapse visualizations, Monsoon & Landslide Sentinel empowers emergency responders and vulnerable communities to act before catastrophic slides or flash floods strike.
details:
OVERVIEW AND HOW IT WORKS

Monsoon & Landslide Sentinel is an early-warning geospatial system designed to detect and forecast monsoon-triggered floods and landslides in real time. Traditional optical satellites cannot see through dense storm clouds precisely when severe monsoons strike. Our solution solves this blind spot using NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR) data.

Our Python-based risk engine processes sequential, cloud-penetrating NISAR L-band radar passes to detect subtle, centimeter-scale ground deformation, soil saturation spikes, and expanding surface water beneath thick forest canopies. To explain the physical mechanics behind slope failure, our model fuses these radar changes with terrain slope angles from the NASA SRTM Digital Elevation Model and 24-hour precipitation triggers from NASA GPM IMERG. The system calculates a weighted Slope Instability Index and categorizes terrain into High, Moderate, or Low hazard zones.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Our primary goal is to turn complex orbital radar datasets into clear, actionable alerts for local disaster management authorities, civil engineers, and vulnerable hillside communities. By identifying steep, water-saturated slopes before catastrophic failure occurs, Monsoon & Landslide Sentinel provides crucial lead time for targeted evacuations, road closures, and infrastructure protection—saving lives during peak monsoon seasons.

TOOLS, LANGUAGES, AND DATA SOURCES

- Programming & Modeling: Python (numpy, rasterio, geopandas) for computing the Slope Instability Index and processing geospatial layers.

- Satellite & Ancillary Datasets: NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar (NISAR L-band and S-band products), NASA SRTM (30m Digital Elevation Model), and NASA GPM IMERG precipitation data.

- Presentation & Documentation: GitHub for open-source code hosting and a 7-slide architectural pitch deck.

CREATIVITY AND KEY DESIGN CONSIDERATIONS

Instead of treating radar imagery as a static visual overlay, we creatively combined dual-frequency radar physics with physical slope-stability mechanics (ground displacement, terrain gradient, soil moisture, and rainfall). When designing the project, our team prioritized:

- All-Weather Cloud Penetration: Ensuring uninterrupted monitoring during heavy monsoon storms when optical satellites fail.

- Canopy Penetration: Leveraging NISAR's 24 cm L-band wavelength to measure bare-earth movement beneath dense tropical vegetation.

- Open-Source Scalability: Structuring the risk model with lightweight, reproducible code so emergency teams in any hilly or flood-prone region worldwide can adapt it quickly.
